subject: AWS Marketplace: proration & entitlement reconciliation for Acme AI SaaS
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: AWS Marketplace Partner Ops <mpx-fulfillments@amazonaws.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace: initial ask — entitlement mapping & proration behavior for Acme AI

Hi team,

Following up on our Marketplace listing for Acme AI (SaaS SaaS-ACME-Prod), we need to confirm a few metering/fulfillment behaviors before we go live:

- Entitlement model: Acme will rely on seat-based entitlements with monthly adjustments (add/remove seats mid-cycle). We need confirmation on how entitlements are reconciled when customers change quantity mid-billing-cycle (proration expectations).
- Metering dimension mapping: please confirm AWS requires a single dimension (active_seats) vs. us sending usage records and separate entitlement events.
- Fulfillment flow: which webhook payloads does AWS expect for entitlement grants vs. usage-based metering? We attached a proposed mapping sheet.

Attachments: saas-mpx-entitlement-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet) — mapping of Redwood SKU -> AWS dimension; proposed-fulfillment-flow.drawio (diagram).

Ask: can Partner Ops provide the exact test payload for entitlement_grant / entitlement_revoke and the recommended approach for proration (AWS-side credit vs. vendor-side invoice adjustments)?

Timeline: Acme wants to begin a closed beta the week of Aug 3. We need test hooks and a sandbox fulfillment URL by 7/26 to run reconciliation tests.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Exec, Marketplace & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: AWS Marketplace Partner Ops <mpx-fulfillments@amazonaws.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: initial ask — entitlement mapping & proration behavior for Acme AI

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the details and the attachment — useful. A few quick notes:

- Proration: AWS Marketplace does not automatically prorate charges for SaaS SaaS contracts at the entitlement level. Typically vendors either (a) issue credits/invoice adjustments to the buyer, or (b) manage a separate usage dimension to reflect pro-rated usage. If you want Marketplace to reflect the change automatically, you need to submit a separate usage event granularity that compensates for partial periods.
- Entitlement model: we support a boolean grant/revoke flow as well as quantity-based entitlements. For quantity-based (active_seats), we expect the entitlement_grant webhook to include the quantity field and a fulfillment_id.
- Test payloads & sandbox: attached sample payloads are available from our partner portal; we'll create a sandbox fulfillment endpoint for you. Please provide the exact JSON schema you'd like to test and your webhook endpoint URL.

I'll loop in our integration engineer if you want live testing.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Partner Ops
mpx-fulfillments@amazonaws.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Partner Ops <mpx-fulfillments@amazonaws.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: initial ask — entitlement mapping & proration behavior for Acme AI

Lena / Acme procurement —

Quick summary of what AWS said and what we recommend:

- We recommend Redwood handle proration on the vendor side and send explicit usage adjustments to AWS when customers change seats mid-cycle. That keeps invoice clarity for Acme and avoids relying on AWS AI credit flows.
- Proposed approach: Redwood will send entitlement_grant with quantity X at the time of subscription, then on mid-cycle changes we will:
  1) send a usage adjustment event for the remainder of the month that reflects the delta in seat-days,
  2) include a metadata field in the usage record referencing your internal invoice id so finance can reconcile.

Attached: saas-mpx-entitlement-mapping.xlsx (mapping + example usage records). Can you confirm Acme's preferred invoice id format and whether your finance team requires net-of-prorate line items or a single monthly net?

DocuSign: legal sent the updated SOW last night. Quick signature would let us set the fulfillment_url in sandbox. Link: https://www.docusign.net/DocuSign/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=dc1234

Next steps we want to land this week:
- Acme confirms invoice id format and proration preference (net-of-prorate line items vs. single net) — Lena
- Redwood to provide sandbox webhook endpoint and JSON schema by 7/22 — Ben
- AWS to stand up sandbox fulfillment URL by 7/26 — AWS Ops

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: initial ask — entitlement mapping & proration behavior for Acme AI

On Tue, Jul 20, 2026 at 10:07 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Lena / Acme procurement —
> 
> Quick summary of what AWS said and what we recommend:
> 
> - We recommend Redwood handle proration on the vendor side and send explicit usage adjustments to AWS when customers change seats mid-cycle. That keeps invoice clarity for Acme and avoids relying on AWS AI credit flows.

Hi Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying items from Acme's finance team:

1) Invoice format: we prefer net-of-prorate line items (so each invoice shows the base subscription line plus a prorate adjustment line). That helps with our internal chargebacks.
2) Invoice IDs: format should be ACME-INV-{YYYYMM}-{SEQ}, e.g., ACME-INV-202608-001. Please ensure the metadata field on the usage adjustment references that string.
3) Billing cadence: monthly, calendar-month aligned. If Redwood sends usage adjustments after month close we need a 5-business-day window for reconciliation.

We'll get the DocuSign signed by EOD 7/21 if everything else lines up. Also cc'ing our engineering contact in case AWS needs test accounts.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Finance, Acme AI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeai.com>, AWS Marketplace Partner Ops <mpx-fulfillments@amazonaws.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: initial ask — entitlement mapping & proration behavior for Acme AI

Thanks everyone — short plan and engineering commitments: 

1) Sandbox webhook: we will stand up a temporary fulfillment endpoint at https://sandbox.redwood.com/mpx/fulfillments/acme that accepts the entitlement_grant / entitlement_update / usage_adjustment payloads. Expect schema by 7/22 COB.
2) Usage schema: we will include an invoice_id metadata field matching ACME-INV-{YYYYMM}-{SEQ} and a prorate_line boolean so finance can split line items.
3) Reconciliation job: Redwood will run a nightly entitlement_reconcile job that compares active_seats vs. AWS reported usage and emits adjustments within the 5-business-day window. We'll provide logs and a reconciliation report to Acme via a shared Drive link.
4) DocuSign: Ben to confirm once signed and then we'll request AWS to flip the fulfillment_url from sandbox -> production.

Action owners: Ben (sandbox + reconcile job), Monica (billing SLA + report format), Soojin (legal / timeline & customer comms).

Attachments referenced: saas-mpx-entitlement-mapping.xlsx, proposed-fulfillment-flow.drawio

I'll follow up with the JSON schema and a sample payload before EOD 7/22.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
